title: A class number abolished and then used again for another job
question: Has Human Resources abolished a job class and later given the same number to a different job, so that the number’s history describes two jobs?
finding: 1 class number in the classification actions of fiscal 2009 to 2027 was established, abolished and established again. Class 0385 was first established as Crime Scene Investigations Manager (fiscal 2016), abolished in fiscal 2024, and established again as Chief of Police (Transitional) (fiscal 2025); the payroll names a holder only in fiscal 2025. A count that dates the class from its first establishment calls the second job nine years old when it was created and filled in the same year.
how: Every class number in the Department of Human Resources’ classification actions, fiscal 2009 to 2027, whose actions run Establish, then Abolish, then Establish again. The first title is the one printed in the notice that established it; the later title is the one printed in the later action or, failing that, the payroll’s.
limits: Reusing a retired number is ordinary bookkeeping and saves renumbering pay tables. It matters only for counts that date a class from its first establishment. The action lists before fiscal 2025 print no titles, so a reuse with no abolition on file would not be seen.

columns.t: Fiscal years with a paid holder
